https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/.text: Military Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Industry Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links WMD Intelligence Homeland Security Space Military Comment by Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova on the situation in Moldova 14 August 2026 14:23 1272-14-08-2026 The Moldovan authorities, infected with the virus of Russophobia, continue to churn out unfounded accusations against our country. On August 5, Moldovan President Maia Sandu, as usual, stated on local television - without a shred of evidence - that the Russian Federation has never abandoned the idea of regaining control of power in the Republic of Moldova. She added that Russia allegedly continues to attempt to destroy everything that has been done to strengthen sovereignty and to ensure that "decisions are made in Moscow, not in Chisinau." These conclusions struck even Moldovans themselves with their sheer cynicism, who noted that no one has done more to undermine the republic's sovereignty than the current authorities, and that all important decisions for the country over the past five years have been made exclusively in Brussels. On August 10, Moldovan leaders, speaking in lockstep, blamed Russia for the incident involving an unidentified drone, after fragments were discovered near Crocmaz, a village in the Stefan Voda District. Despite the lack of reliable information about the drone's origin, Moldovan authorities, well versed in distracting the population from their own governance failures, seized the opportunity to stage a charade, culminating in the urgent recall of their ambassador from Moscow to Chisinau for consultations. This scenario is not new. Last month, Romanian authorities also recalled their ambassador from Moscow after a similar incident involving an allegedly Russian drone. Clearly, both were working from the same playbook in their attempts to pin the blame for their failures on our country. Today, the Chisinau regime's only claim to fame is a rapidly deteriorating socioeconomic situation, as well as the deepening crises in the environmental and energy sectors. Struggling to stay afloat, the authorities had to abandon the announced salary increases for public sector employees and raise VAT rates on grain and oilseed crops from 8 to 12 percent - a move that will primarily hit small and medium-sized farms. Incidentally, local farmers are barely surviving in the midst of the harvest season due to rising prices for diesel fuel (up to 70 percent) and fertiliser (by 35-40 percent). Even the huge financial injections from the European Union into the country's economy have failed to improve the situation. Meanwhile, the Sandu regime always seems to find money for military purposes. On August 5, the Moldovan Government approved the 2026-2030 Implementation Programme for the National Defence Strategy, which proposes strengthening the country's defence capability by increasing military spending to 1 percent of GDP, as well as gradual integration into the security and defence structures of the European Union. Patently anti-people initiatives are also being implemented in the domestic political sphere. Here are a few examples. The government continues settling scores with the legally elected head of Gagauzia, Evghenia Guțul. Media reports have emerged that, right before the first anniversary of her serving the unprecedentedly harsh seven-year sentence handed down in August 2025, she was transferred from Chisinau to Penitentiary Institution No. 7 in the village of Rusca, known for its inhumane conditions. Guțul's lawyer reported that prisoners there even face a shortage of running water, and its quality leaves much to be desired. The authorities, following the patterns of the Kiev Nazis, are continuing their efforts to artificially de-Russify Moldova's information landscape. On July 31, at the initiative of deputies from the ruling Action and Solidarity party, a bill amending the Code on Audiovisual Media Services was submitted to the Parliament of the Republic. The amendments codify the concept of "disinformation," introduce a mandatory requirement for broadcasters to air at least 50 percent of their programming in Romanian or dubbed into Romanian between 6:00 am and midnight, and add a separate chapter to the Code regulating the activities of the regional public broadcaster of Gagauzia. The Moldovan authorities continue to fight the Soviet legacy they hate so much. For example, in late July, the country's Ministry of Defence dismantled two artillery pieces from the Great Patriotic War at the central entrance to the ministry. The legendary installations were one of the symbols of the Great Victory over Nazism and had stood in their places for decades. They have apparently become an irritant for the current "defenders" of the Republic. It is telling that their EU handlers turn a blind eye to all the totalitarian manifestations in modern Moldova, where the principles of the rule of law are trampled, and repression of political opponents and the purging of the information space have become commonplace. Apparently, these are the true "European values" the Sandu regime is prepared to fight for - even at the expense of its own country's prosperity. Ordinary Moldovans, trapped by the anti-Russia course pursued by official Chisinau, are paying the price for such actions.
